findings.text: The `command:<name>` event used to be emitted on the command itself (`this.emit`). It is now emitted only on `this.parent`, and only when a parent exists. Any listener registered on the command for its own `command:<name>` event no longer fires. For the root program with an action handler, the event is never emitted at all.

0.reason: Moving the `command:<name>` emit to `this.parent` is a deliberate change, marked `// legacy` in the patch: it brings back the older Commander behaviour where the parent program listens for `command:<sub>` (for example `program.on('command:foo')`). Dropping the emit on the command itself and on the root program is therefore by design, and this is not the reference unknown-option ordering bug.
